text:
# kanevskyy.dev

Personal static site (portfolio + blog), built with a small custom Node script. No framework.

## Build

- Do NOT run `npm run build`, `npm run watch`, or any tests — building and testing are handled separately by the user. Just edit the source files.
- For reference: `build.js` generates `dist/` from the sources below; `npm run watch` rebuilds on change (Node `--watch-path`); `npm run serve` runs `serve.js`, a zero-dependency static server (Node built-ins only) that serves `dist/` at `http://localhost:3000` with directory→`index.html` fallback. Run `watch` and `serve` in two terminals during development: edit a source file → `watch` rebuilds `dist/` → refresh the browser.

## Structure

- `homepage.html`, `privacy.html` — static pages copied as-is to `dist/index.html` and `dist/privacy/index.html`. They do NOT use the template, so `<head>` changes must be made in each of them separately.
- `templates/base.html` — template with `{{TITLE}}`/`{{DESCRIPTION}}`/`{{CONTENT}}`/`{{YEAR}}` placeholders, used only for generated blog/project pages.
- `posts/*.md`, `projects/*.md` — markdown with gray-matter frontmatter (`title`, `description`, `date`, optional `slug`) → `dist/blog/<slug>/` and `dist/projects/<slug>/`.
- `tools/` — standalone self-contained HTML tools, copied wholesale to `dist/tools/`. Each tool lives in its own subdirectory as `index.html` (e.g. `tools/placeholder/index.html` → `dist/tools/placeholder/`). Not processed by build.js beyond a recursive copy. Each tool is fully self-contained: it must NOT link `/assets/style.css` or any shared site stylesheet — all markup, styles, and scripts live inline in the tool's own HTML. `tools/index.html` is the listing page (that one does use the site template/styling and is manually maintained). New tools need an entry added to that listing.
- `assets/` — copied wholesale to `dist/assets/`; new static files (favicon, images) just go here, no build.js change needed.

## Environment notes

- Windows; no ImageMagick or sharp available. For image resizing use PowerShell `System.Drawing`.
- `HANDOFF.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are gitignored on purpose.


## Additional notes

- Make heavy use of subagents (sync parallel preferred) when possible — it minimizes work time and prevents cascading state issues.
- For canvas gallery effects, always use the `delegate` agent for individual file edits.
- All interactive effects MUST have a `mouseleave` handler that resets `c._mx`/`c._my` to sentinel values.
- Effect sizes and positions should always scale with canvas dimensions (`w, h` in draw, `c.canvas.width/2` in init).
- Hardcoded pixel values (e.g. `Math.random()*800`) are bugs — they must be relative to canvas size.
- For performance on upscaled canvases, use adaptive step sizes: `Math.max(3, Math.ceil(Math.min(w,h)*0.006))`.
- `HANDOFF.md` contains the current gallery state with all pending tasks.

## Canvas Gallery conventions

- **Tags**: `'interactive'` = responds to mouse, `'particles'` = particle system, `'generative'` = procedural, `'geometry'` = shapes, `'retro'` = classic
- **Interactive effects**: store `c._mx, c._my` via `c._evt` mousemove handler, `c._evtd` mouseleave handler, destroy removes both listeners
- **Init/draw convention**: `function(c)` for init, `function(c,w,h,t)` for draw. `w,h` = CSS pixel dimensions, `t` = ms since first draw call
- **Performance**: Use `c._first` flag for one-time setup in draw. Use `c._init` pattern for deferred init that depends on `w,h`
- **Destroy**: Must clean up ALL event listeners (mousemove + mouseleave) to prevent memory leaks

-1 (function(){register('Boids','A flocking simulation where colorful birds swarm around your cursor.','interactive',function(c){c._boids=[];c._mx=0;c._my=0;c._evtd=function(){c._mx=-9999;c._my=-9999};for(var i=0;i<80;i++)c._boids.push({x:Math.random()*600,y:Math.random()*400,vx:(Math.random()-.5)*2,vy:(Math.random()-.5)*2});c._evt=function(e){var r=c.canvas.getBoundingClientRect();c._mx=e.clientX-r.left;c._my=e.clientY-r.top};c.canvas.addEventListener('mousemove',c._evt);c.canvas.addEventListener('mouseleave',c._evtd)},function(c,w,h,t){c.fillStyle='rgba(0,0,0,.08)';c.fillRect(0,0,w,h);var b=c._boids;for(var i=0;i<b.length;i++){var bx=0,by=0,ax=0,ay=0,cx=0,cy=0,count=0;for(var j=0;j<b.length;j++){if(i===j)continue;var dx=b[j].x-b[i].x,dy=b[j].y-b[i].y,d=Math.hypot(dx,dy)||1;if(d<40){bx-=dx/d;by-=dy/d}if(d<100){ax+=dx;ay+=dy;count++}}if(count){ax=ax/count-b[i].vx;ay=ay/count-b[i].vy;ax*=.005;ay*=.005}bx*=.03;by*=.03;cx=(c._mx-b[i].x)*.003;cy=(c._my-b[i].y)*.003;var f=1-Math.hypot(c._mx-b[i].x,c._my-b[i].y)/600;if(f<0)f=0;cx*=f;cy*=f;b[i].vx+=ax+bx+cx;b[i].vy+=ay+by+cy;var sp=Math.hypot(b[i].vx,b[i].vy)||1;if(sp>4){b[i].vx=b[i].vx/sp*4;b[i].vy=b[i].vy/sp*4}b[i].x+=b[i].vx;b[i].y+=b[i].vy;if(b[i].x<0)b[i].x=w;if(b[i].x>w)b[i].x=0;if(b[i].y<0)b[i].y=h;if(b[i].y>h)b[i].y=0;var ang=Math.atan2(b[i].vy,b[i].vx)+Math.PI/2;c.save();c.translate(b[i].x,b[i].y);c.rotate(ang);c.fillStyle='#fff';c.beginPath();c.moveTo(0,-6);c.lineTo(-4,4);c.lineTo(4,4);c.closePath();c.fill();c.restore()}},function(c){try{c.canvas.removeEventListener('mousemove',c._evt);c.canvas.removeEventListener('mouseleave',c._evtd)}catch(e){}},'Each bird follows three simple rules: alignment with neighbors, cohesion toward the group center, and separation to avoid collisions.');})();
